title: Longest Cycle in a Graph
summary: Given a directed graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where each node has at most one outgoing edge, represented by an array of size n, find the length of the longest cycle.
statement: Given a directed graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where each node has at most one outgoing edge, represented by an array of size n, find the length of the longest cycle. If no cycle exists, return -1. A cycle is defined as a path that starts and ends at the same node.
constraints: edges has 2 through 100000 entries; edges[i] is -1 or one outgoing neighbor distinct from i.
Return the number of vertices in the longest directed cycle.
Return -1 when the graph has no cycle.
hints: A cycle counts only when the current walk revisits one of its own nodes.
Keep both global visited state and a map from current-walk nodes to their step index.
Walk outgoing edges until -1 or a visited node; if that endpoint is in the current map, subtract its first step.
Outdegree at most one makes each start a single path, and global marking ensures every vertex is processed once.
editorial: Outdegree at most one makes each start a single path, and global marking ensures every vertex is processed once.

tests.explanation: Vertices two, four, and three form a directed cycle of length three.
Every path eventually reaches node one and stops, so there is no cycle.
